name: LHAASO
full_name: Large High Altitude Air Shower Observatory
summary: High-altitude cosmic-ray observatory that studies cosmic-ray origins and uses high-energy gamma rays to constrain superheavy dark-matter decay and annihilation.
detection_principle: Combines a ground electromagnetic-particle array, muon detectors, a water-Cherenkov array and wide-field Cherenkov telescopes to reconstruct extensive air showers and distinguish photons from hadrons.

status.label: Operation supported by evidence
status.evidence: The IHEP facility directory explicitly lists the observatory as “In Operation.”

key_parameters.name: Dark-matter mass range in the 2022 analysis
key_parameters.value: 10^5–10^9 GeV; not the detector's energy coverage for all particle species

results.summary: No dark-matter excess was found in 570 days of data; lower limits were placed on heavy dark-matter lifetimes.
Dwarf-spheroidal-galaxy observations constrain the properties of superheavy dark matter.

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
